name: Inter-State supply
definition: A supply is in the course of inter-State trade or commerce when s.7 of the IGST Act says it is. For goods, s.7(1) — subject to s.10 — the location of the supplier and the place of supply are in two different States, two different Union territories, or a State and a Union territory. For services, s.7(3) applies the same three-limb test, subject to s.12. Section 7 also treats as inter-State, without any comparison of locations: goods imported into the territory of India till they cross the customs frontiers of India (s.7(2)); services imported into the territory of India (s.7(4)); and under s.7(5) a supply where the supplier is located in India and the place of supply is outside India, a supply to or by a Special Economic Zone developer or unit, and a supply in the taxable territory not being an intra-State supply and not covered elsewhere in that section.
why_it_exists: It is the single fact that decides WHICH tax is charged. IGST s.5(1) levies integrated tax on inter-State supplies; CGST s.9(1) levies central tax on intra-State supplies. Getting this wrong does not misstate an amount — it charges the wrong tax to the wrong government, and no rate check catches it because the number can be identical.
inputs: the place of supply, determined first under s.10 for goods and s.12 for services
whether the goods were imported into the territory of India and whether they have crossed the customs frontiers of India
whether the service was imported into the territory of India
whether either party is a Special Economic Zone developer or a Special Economic Zone unit
whether the supply is in the taxable territory
outputs: a determination that the supply IS or IS NOT in the course of inter-State trade or commerce
or an escalation, where the location of the supplier or the place of supply cannot be established on the evidence held
preconditions: the transaction is a supply under s.7 of the CGST Act (GST-SUPPLY-SCOPE)

the place of supply has ALREADY been determined — s.7(1) and s.7(3) are expressly subject to s.10 and s.12, so the comparison cannot be made before the place of supply exists (GST-POS-GOODS, GST-POS-SERVICES-INDIA)
it is known whether the supply is of goods or of services, because s.7(1) and s.7(3) are separate limbs
exceptions: goods imported into India, till they cross the customs frontiers of India — s.7(2), inter-State regardless of locations
services imported into India — s.7(4), inter-State regardless of locations
supplier in India and place of supply outside India — s.7(5)(a)
a supply to or by a Special Economic Zone developer or unit — s.7(5)(b), and correspondingly excluded from intra-State supply by the provisos to s.8(1) and s.8(2)
the residual limb — a supply in the taxable territory, not being an intra-State supply and not covered elsewhere in s.7 — s.7(5)(c)
UNKNOWN — s.9 of the IGST Act (supplies in territorial waters) is a further special case and has not been extracted here
UNKNOWN — source is the IGST Act as on 23-05-2025; later amendments not held locally
common_mistakes: comparing the supplier's State with the RECIPIENT's State — s.7(1) and s.7(3) compare the location of the supplier with the PLACE OF SUPPLY, which is not always where the recipient is
making the comparison before determining the place of supply — both limbs are expressly subject to s.10 and s.12
treating a supply to a Special Economic Zone unit inside the same State as intra-State — s.7(5)(b) makes it inter-State and the provisos to s.8 exclude it
treating imported goods as intra-State because the importer and the port are in one State — s.7(2) settles it before any location is compared
reading the residual limb in s.7(5)(c) as a general catch-all — it applies only in the taxable territory and only where the supply is not already covered elsewhere in s.7
dependencies: UNKNOWN — the IGST Act defines 'location of the supplier of services' (s.2(15)) but defines NO 'location of the supplier of goods'. The goods limb of s.7(1) therefore rests on a term the Act does not define, and no substitute may be invented here.
legal_references: IGST Act, 2017 s.10 — referenced by s.7(1)
IGST Act, 2017 s.12 — referenced by s.7(3)
IGST Act, 2017 s.15 — referenced by the proviso to s.8(1); NOT extracted
IGST Act, 2017 s.9 — supplies in territorial waters; NOT extracted
icai_references: NOT APPLICABLE — whether a supply is inter-State is a question of statutory charge, not of accounting measurement. No Accounting Standard speaks to it.
evidence_required: the location of the supplier, evidenced by the place of business from which the supply was made
the place of supply as determined under s.10 or s.12, with the limb relied on named
for imported goods: the bill of entry and the date the goods crossed the customs frontiers of India
for a Special Economic Zone counterparty: proof of developer or unit status
confidence_factors: zero until the place of supply has been determined — the whole test is subject to s.10 and s.12
weak for goods, because 'location of the supplier' is undefined in the Act for goods; only 'location of the supplier of services' is defined, at s.2(15)
weak when Special Economic Zone status is asserted but not evidenced — it flips the answer regardless of geography
UNKNOWN — s.9 (territorial waters) and s.15 (tourist) were not extracted, so supplies touching them cannot be closed from this concept
validation_checks: the place of supply is determined and recorded BEFORE the inter-State test is applied
the comparison recorded is supplier location against PLACE OF SUPPLY, never against the recipient's address
a Special Economic Zone supply is never classified intra-State, whatever the two locations are
an inter-State determination and an intra-State determination are never both recorded for one supply
the limb of s.7 relied on is named in the determination
examples: goods moved from a supplier's place of business in one State to a recipient in another; the place of supply under s.10(1)(a) is where the movement terminates, that State differs from the supplier's, so s.7(1)(a) is satisfied and the supply is inter-State
goods imported into India and still inside the customs frontiers — s.7(2) treats the supply as inter-State without any location being compared
counterexamples: a supplier and a recipient in the same State where the goods are delivered to a third person's principal place of business in another State — the place of supply under s.10(1)(b) is that other State, so the supply is inter-State even though supplier and recipient share a State
a supply to a Special Economic Zone unit situated in the supplier's own State — the two locations coincide, yet s.7(5)(b) makes it inter-State
